name: Oil (Brent)
summary: Brent near $94 on 5 Nov after a sharp weekly fall; Alert holds while Hormuz stays largely shut
state: Brent fell 4.7% to $98.76 on 4 Nov, below $100 for the first time since early October, and traded near $93.6 early on 5 Nov on hopes of a US–Iran deal, a price in the Watch band (Gulf News). Alert is kept on the physical outage: Iran still ties reopening Hormuz to an end to the US blockade and sanctions relief, and the IRGC claimed on 5 Nov that two tankers and a tug caught fire in the strait (The National).
for_you: Fuel and transport costs remain exposed to Gulf supply; prices have swung by several dollars a day on war and talks news since 3 Nov.
rubric_hit: Hormuz largely shut: major physical outage > 2 mb/d = Alert (price $93.6 in Watch band)
basis_detail: raised above the data floor on reported events

sources.title: Gulf News — Iran warns against war as Trump signals 'heavy hit' and tankers catch fire near Hormuz
The National — Iran war latest: IRGC claims two tankers and tugboat caught fire in Strait of Hormuz

why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
